ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism (Act No. 18986, as amended) and the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 18987, as amended), together with the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Recommendations as implemented by the Financial Services Commission.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies in the beneficial owner's jurisdiction (e.g., Companies House, Hong Kong Companies Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille by the competent authority of the issuing country if a party to the Hague Apostille Convention; otherwise, consular legalization by the Embassy of the Republic of Korea in the issuing country.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies in the beneficial owner's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille by the competent authority of the issuing country if a party to the Hague Apostille Convention; otherwise, consular legalization by the Embassy of the Republic of Korea in the issuing country.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the beneficial owner entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a notary public in the issuing country, followed by apostille or consular legalization as applicable.
Notarization by a notary public in the issuing country, followed by apostille or consular legalization as applicable.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories must undergo enhanced due diligence screening against the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) consolidated list, the United Nations Security Council sanctions lists, the Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list, and the Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) domestic watchlist. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) are identified using a risk-based approach, with mandatory enhanced monitoring for foreign PEPs, their family members, and close associates. Screening must be conducted at onboarding and on an ongoing basis, with alerts escalated to the compliance officer for review. Any positive match requires immediate suspension of the incorporation process and filing a suspicious transaction report (STR) with KoFIU within 24 hours.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea, Registry Office (Internet Registration Office, i-register)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be in Korean (Hangul). A romanized version may be registered for international use but must be consistent with the Korean name. The name must include the corporate form suffix '주식회사' (Chusik Hoesa). The name must be distinguishable from existing registered names and must not contain prohibited words. Transliteration of foreign names must follow the Revised Romanization of Korean system.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name application is rejected, the applicant may file an administrative appeal with the Supreme Court Registry Office within 14 days of the rejection notice. The appeal must include a written explanation of why the name should be accepted, along with supporting evidence. The Registry Office must render a decision within 30 days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Administrative Court. Alternatively, the applicant may submit a new name application with a modified name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are permissible for registered agent and secretarial services, provided a physical address is registered for service of legal process and official correspondence. However, the Korean National Tax Service and local banks may reject virtual offices for tax registration and banking compliance, especially for entities in high-risk industries. A physical office with a dedicated mailbox and staff is strongly recommended to satisfy commercial substance requirements and avoid adverse tax assessments.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) Registered office must be a physical address within South Korea; (2) The office must display the company name; (3) The office must have a reception area and staff; (4) The company must maintain books and records at the office; (5) The company must have a designated address for official notices. Risk of unannounced physical inspection by municipal tax authorities or the registry is moderate, estimated at 15% annual probability for entities in the registered agent sector, given heightened scrutiny of shell companies.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Articles 288 through 317 inclusive, together with Articles 340, 365 through 368, 383 through 393, and 416 as applicable to incorporation, capital subscription, registered office, and statutory officer appointment of a Chusik Hoesa (Stock Corporation).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Commercial Registration Section, Registry Office of the Seoul Central District Court, or the competent local court Registry Office in the judicial district where the corporate seat is established.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation registration application submitted with the Notarized Articles of Incorporation, together with the supporting subscription and capital payment statements, filed under the Commercial Act and the Regulation on Commercial Registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed under the Korean Commercial Act for a Chusik Hoesa; however, where the Articles of Incorporation subscribe a positive capital amount, the full issue price must be paid into a Korean real-name bank account in the name of the corporation before the incorporation registration application is filed. The Registry Office will require a certificate of payment, deposit, or remittance from the bank. No blocked escrow account is legally mandatory, but actual payment must be fully completed and evidenced before registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST MEETING OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [CHUSIK HOESA], a stock corporation proposed to be organized under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea. The undersigned, being all the directors validly designated by the incorporators, waive notice of this meeting and unanimously adopt the following resolutions. 1. SUBSCRIPTION OF SHARE CAPITAL. RESOLVED, that this board acknowledges the lawfully subscribed shares of the corporation and the full payment, deposit, or remittance of the aggregate subscription price by the subscribers or promoters before the filing of incorporation registration; that the directors are authorized to allot and issue shares, prepare the shareholder register, and complete all steps required by Articles 288 through 317 of the Commercial Act; and that the directors shall cause the corporation to maintain proper records of paid-in capital and any non-cash contributions with the required appraiser reports. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED, that the directors are authorized to open, operate, and maintain demand deposit, settlement, foreign currency, and payment collection accounts in the name of the corporation at one or more commercial banks in the Republic of Korea; to sign and file account opening applications, signature cards, electronic banking mandates, wire transfer authorizations, and banking resolutions; and to appoint any director or officer as sole or joint authorized signatory subject to applicable anti-money-laundering procedures. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the corporation shall be located within the Republic of Korea at the address specified in the Articles of Incorporation; that the registered agent and secretarial office may operate at that address or at a licensed service provider address; and that the directors shall file any future change of registered office with the competent Registry Office and publish or register all notices required by law. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS. RESOLVED, that the following persons are hereby appointed to serve for the initial term: the Representative Director, the Corporate Secretary, the Compliance Officer, and the Registered Agent Coordinator, each with authority to execute, certify, submit, and receive documents on behalf of the corporation, to attend registrations, to appear before public authorities, and to exercise all powers necessary for the corporate secretarial and registered agent business contemplated under ISIC 8299. 5. GENERAL COVER. RESOLVED, that the officers and directors are further authorized to prepare, notarize, apostille, and file all regulatory declarations, tax registrations, professional license applications, and third-party consents needed to lawfully commence the companys business and to complete any ministerial act that the board may lawfully delegate. These resolutions are effective immediately upon the date of incorporation registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation, Articles Drafting, and Notarization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internet Registry Office of the Supreme Court of Korea and a Korean Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Korean-language Articles of Incorporation containing the corporate name, business purpose, registered office location, number and par value of authorized shares, total shares to be issued at incorporation, and ordinary notice method. Reserve the proposed corporate name with the Internet Registry Office of the Supreme Court of Korea and obtain the name reservation certificate. After the incorporators have executed the articles, the entire document must be notarized by a Korea notary public. Where a foreign corporate shareholder is involved, the shareholder must supply legalized or apostilled constitutional documents, board authorization, and passport or director identification; if the company will outsource secretarial services, the registered agent contract may be prepared at this stage.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID copies of all incorporators
Power of attorney executed by incorporators
Certificate of corporate registration and board resolution if a corporate body is an incorporator
Foreign entity constitutional documents and register extract, apostilled or legalized
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit a new reservation request with a different Korean corporate name. If the notary or the Registry pre-screening requires amendments, re-execute and re-notarize the amended articles and resubmit the same package without losing priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription and Deposit into a Korean Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: A commercial bank licensed as a foreign exchange bank in the Republic of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary subscription or designated corporate suspense account in South Korea in the name of the corporation or its promoters and ensure each subscriber remits the full subscription price in Korean won or another freely convertible currency. Obtain an official certificate of deposit, account balance confirmation, or remittance receipt from the bank showing the corporates name and the deposited amount. If any contribution is in kind, secure an appraiser valuation report and an assignment instrument. The bank must be instructed to release the funds only after incorporation registration is completed or as permitted under the Commercial Act and foreign exchange regulations. This step is essential because the Registry Office will reject a filing without proof of actual payment.
required_dossiers: Application for corporate deposit account opening
Provisional or final Articles of Incorporation
Subscriber or promoter list with subscribed shares
Certificate of directors appointment to act as signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank reports a foreign-exchange consent issue or refusal, obtain the relevant Ministry of Economy and Finance or designated bank approval under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act or choose another licensed bank and repeat the deposit process with corrected documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Incorporation Registration at the Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registration Section of the local Registry Office having jurisdiction over the corporate seat, including Seoul Central District Court Registry Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within two weeks after completion of capital payment and appointment of directors and auditor, file the incorporation registration with the Registry Office by electronic internet filing or in-person submission. The application must show the corporate name, purpose, principal business address, directors, representative director, auditor where applicable, and subscribed capital. Attach the notarized Articles of Incorporation, capital deposit certificate, report on appointment of directors, written consents of directors and auditor to serve, specimen seal card, and proof of registration tax and local education tax payment. The court examines the application for legal conformity; once accepted, the corporation is deemed incorporated as of the registration date and a Certificate of Incorporation is issued.
required_dossiers: Certificate of paid-in capital or deposit receipt
Report on appointment of directors and auditor
Written acceptance of office signed by each director
Proof of payment of court registration fees and local education tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a correction order, submit the requested corrected documents before the statutory deadline. If registration is suspended, file a written explanation with supporting evidence and request review by the chief registrar; judicial objection is available through the court if the registry refuses to register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Tax Registration and Business License Posting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Tax Office of the National Tax Service and the municipal business administration office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Certificate of Incorporation, promptly file the business registration certificate application with the National Tax Service through the Home Tax Service portal or the local district tax office. Obtain the corporate registration number, business start date, taxpayer status, and any required VAT registration. File the corporate seal registration, obtain a digital certificate, and if employees are engaged, register with the National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, and Employment Insurance system. The company should also obtain a basic office occupancy certificate from the relevant local government to evidence lawful business premises for the registered agent and secretarial office. Because ISIC 8299 is a regulated service business, the operating license must be maintained before executing client contracts.
required_dossiers: Business premises lease agreement or ownership certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the National Tax Service flags incomplete information, correct the return and submit supporting leases, IDs, and certificate of incorporation. For refusal of business registration, appeal administratively to the high tax office within the statutory objection period or reapply after curing the irregularity.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Licensed Registered Agent and Off-Shore Secretarial Operation Approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal Services Industry Division of the Ministry of Justice, together with the local municipal licensing desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the specific administrative license to conduct statutory company secretarial and commercial registered agent services in South Korea. The application must demonstrate a licensed physical office, professional indemnity insurance, an anti-money-laundering compliance program, personal data protection procedures, and employment of a qualified compliance officer or licensed administrative secretary. Submit the certificate of incorporation, articles, business plan, office lease, insurance binder, and criminal background certificates for key personnel. Upon conditional approval, submit any requested supplement within the given period and pay the administrative fee. Receipt of the license is a precondition to onboarding corporate clients for secretarial representation services.
required_dossiers: Business registration certificate from the National Tax Service
Office lease and occupational safety registration
Criminal background certificates of directors and compliance officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the license is objected to or suspended, provide supplementary proof of qualifications, remediation of workplace safety issues, or revised AML policies within the administrative cure period; if final rejection occurs, reconsider with an amended application or pursue judicial review in the administrative court.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Legal Services Industry Division, Ministry of Justice of the Republic of Korea, and the local auxiliary licensing window of the National Tax Service business registration office.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Corporate Secretarial and Commercial Registered Agent Service Provider License, including authorization to act as off-shore registered agent, company secretary, and statutory filing intermediary under Korean corporate law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable for ISIC 8299; the service business has no manufacturing plant, chemical process, assembly line, or warehousing operation requiring a permit from the Ministry of Environment or designated Provincial Environmental Agency.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - No Environmental Impact Assessment registration tier applies to a pure corporate secretarial and registered-agent office. If a future physical facility is established, the then-current EIA category will be determined.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - no wastewater, VOC, hazardous waste, or stack emission discharge thresholds apply to this office-based activity. Any future small business office shall, if renovated, comply with the Clean Air Conservation Act and Water Quality Preservation Act general duties applicable to non-industrial premises.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Basic office occupancy fire safety inspection and certificate of the National Fire Agency, together with workplace safety registration under the Occupational Safety and Health Act with the Korea Occupational Safety and Health Agency; no hazardous chemical storage permit or civil-defense industrial fire permit is required because the activity is administrative and non-industrial.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea, with the electronic tax administration portal HomeTax (hometax.go.kr); electronic VAT e-invoice processing is integrated into HomeTax, while customs clearance is administered by the Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS electronic clearance system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign non-resident entity that establishes or owns a Korean Chusik Hoesa, or that creates a domestic place of business through a registered agent office, the tax identification procedure is as follows. Step 1: Prepare the constituent documents of the foreign entity, including certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation, certificate of foreign registration, power of attorney naming a Korean tax representative, and evidence of the domestic place of business. Step 2: Determine the competent District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the registered business address in Korea. Step 3: File the business registration application prescribed by the National Tax Service through HomeTax or by physical submission at the competent District Tax Office; for a foreign corporation, the filing is made for the Korean branch or domestic place of business using the foreign corporation taxpayer registration procedure. Step 4: Provide supporting documentation proving the existence of the Korean place of business, such as an office lease agreement, registered agent service agreement, and the appointment of a resident responsible person. Step 5: Upon successful review, the NTS issues a Business Registration Certificate containing the ten-digit Business Registration Number, which functions as both the corporate tax identification number and the VAT identifier for the entity. Step 6: Register the entity in the HomeTax e-tax invoice system so that electronic tax invoices can be issued and received. Step 7: If the foreign non-resident entity supplies electronic services or digital content into Korea but has no domestic place of business, the entity must complete the simplified VAT registration procedure available to non-resident suppliers in HomeTax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The Korean Chusik Hoesa is a domestic stock corporation taxed as a separate resident corporation on its worldwide income; it is not eligible for pass-through treatment. For indirect tax purposes, the entity is treated as a VAT-registered taxable business person.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None available for entity classification. Korean corporate tax law does not provide a check-the-box pass-through election for a Chusik Hoesa. Hybrid mismatch adjustments are governed by the Korean Adjustment of International Taxes Act and are applied in accordance with OECD BEPS Action 2 outcomes, but there is no elective hybrid mismatch regime.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: None. Korea requires mandatory VAT registration upon the commencement of any business activity, regardless of turnover level. A simplified taxpayer regime applies to very small domestic suppliers with annual revenue below KRW 80 million, but that regime affects the method of VAT calculation and does not exempt the supplier from registration. Non-resident suppliers without a domestic place of business that provide electronically supplied services or digital products to non-registered Korean recipients may be required to register through the simplified non-resident VAT registration procedure.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea does not operate a real-time third-party fiscal clearance or central anti-fraud stamping system. However, every VAT-registered supplier must issue an electronic tax invoice for all business-to-business supplies and transmit the e-tax invoice to the National Tax Service through HomeTax by no later than the day following the supply date. The e-tax invoice must be in the prescribed XML format and must include the registration numbers of the supplier and recipient, supply value, VAT amount, and supply date. Cash receipts must be issued through the approved cash receipt device for business-to-consumer transactions. The NTS cross-matches e-tax invoice data with customs declarations, bank remittance data, and cash receipt records to detect missing or fraudulent invoices. Failure to issue or transmit e-tax invoices on time attracts additional VAT penalties under the VAT Act.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods from Korea qualify for the 0% VAT rate where the goods are physically removed from Korea under a valid export declaration accepted by the Korea Customs Service and are supported by transport documentation evidencing departure from Korea. Services, including registered agent and company secretarial services supplied to non-resident business clients, qualify for zero-rating where the recipient is a non-resident or a foreign business without a domestic place of business, the service is performed under a written agreement, and the benefit of the service is consumed or used outside Korea. For cross-border digital content or offshore secretarial services, zero-rating additionally requires evidence that payment for the service is received from abroad in a permitted foreign exchange form and that the service would not be physically performed inside Korea for a Korean domestic benefit. Input VAT incurred in connection with zero-rated exports is fully creditable and refundable.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration filed through the UNI-PASS electronic clearance system and accepted by Korea Customs Service
Bill of Lading for sea freight or Air Waybill for air freight evidencing physical departure from Korea
Commercial invoice and packing list corresponding exactly to the exported goods
Bank-issued Foreign Exchange Settlement Confirmation or Inward Remittance Certificate evidencing receipt of export proceeds in a permissible foreign currency
Service contract and supporting correspondence for zero-rated offshore services, including evidence of the non-resident recipient status and overseas place of use
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rated export claims are subject to joint audit scrutiny by the National Tax Service and Korea Customs Service. Where the claimed export is found to be a domestic supply, where the goods do not physically leave Korea, where the foreign exchange proceeds are not received within the applicable statutory repatriation period, or where the supporting documentation is forged, inadequate, or inconsistent, the NTS will deny the 0% VAT rate and assess output VAT at the standard 10% rate on the original supply value. In addition, the taxpayer may be subject to VAT additional penalties for unfiled or understated taxes, late payment interest, correction of corporate income tax in the event of concealed revenue, and refund clawback with interest. Fraudulent zero-rating or false claim of export may be reported to the public prosecutor's office for criminal tax proceedings under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, and responsible officers may be subject to imprisonment or fines.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: The Bank of Korea (BOK), acting under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the delegated supervisory framework of the Ministry of Economy and Finance
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a largely free-floating current-account convertibility regime under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and its Enforcement Decree. Residents and non-residents can settle trade and service payments in convertible currencies through licensed foreign exchange banks; current-account items such as royalties, salaries, intercompany services, dividends, and legal professional fees are not subject to prior approval, provided the underlying contract or invoice is retained for AML and FX reporting. Capital-account convertibility is liberalized but monitored: inbound equity subscriptions, external borrowings, overseas investments, and property purchases require ex-post or prior reports to the Bank of Korea, the Ministry of Economy and Finance or KOTRA, depending on amount and counterparty. Currency conversion is allowed at the market rate without surrender requirements on export proceeds, but all foreign currency receipts must flow into an authorized domestic foreign-exchange bank account, and amounts above a filing threshold are reported through the bank. Profit remittance hurdles are practical rather than exchange-control walls: the company must demonstrate distributable earnings with audited financial statements, board-approved dividend resolutions, and tax clearance documentation; a 20% withholding rate applies on dividends, reduced by the applicable Korea-OECD double tax treaty and a beneficial-ownership certificate. In practice, outbound dividend wires are cleared within one banking day after tax statement filing, as long as the remittance purpose code and shareholding registry are verified.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender ratio is imposed on Korean exporters. Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, an exporter must receive foreign currency proceeds into a designated domestic foreign-exchange bank account by the contractual payment due date, and the ultimate collection period generally must not exceed one year from the date of the export declaration, extendable to fifteen months under documented extenuating circumstances. For receipts exceeding the FX reporting threshold, commonly USD 50,000 equivalent, the foreign exchange bank is obliged to report the transfer through the BOK-reporting system within five business days. Exporters may retain the funds as foreign-currency deposits or convert them into KRW at the prevailing market rate; no fixed percentage must be converted.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Korean Won operating account, foreign currency demand deposit, and capital escrow sub-account
Enterprise demand deposit in KRW and multi-currency foreign exchange deposit accounts for settlement and hedging
Corporate basic operational currency account, trade settlement account, and foreign currency trust ledger
Onshore KRW operating account, foreign currency current account, and capital verification escrow account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Non-viable as primary clearing provider. Under Korean law, only a bank licensed as a foreign-exchange bank under the Korean banking regulatory framework can receive export proceeds, process KRW clearing, and issue BOK FX reports. Offshore fintech EMIs such as Wise, Revolut Business, Airwallex, or Ebury do not hold a Korean banking licence and are not permitted to open an in-denomination KRW settlement account for a Korean legal entity or to perform capital verification. Such EMIs may be used only where a licensed Korean bank permits them as an auxiliary upstream remittance channel for small-value outbound invoices, and even then the underlying transaction must be booked on the Korean bank's system to satisfy regulatory reporting.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The mandated rule is in-branch physical appearance of at least one natural-person account signatory in the Republic of Korea. Korean tier-1 banks will require the statutory representative director, or a locally appointed manager holding an explicit board resolution and a notarized/apostilled power of attorney, to attend a face-to-face KYC interview at a domestic branch. Pure consular proxy opening, where no representative physically enters Korea, is not accepted for a medium-risk corporate with offshore secretarial ownership. A video-call confirmation may complement, but never replace, the physical interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered-agent pass-through structure: the applicant is controlled through a foreign secretarial provider and appears to lack domestic business substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete organizational chart from each ultimate beneficial owner down to the applicant; notarized and apostilled board resolutions appointing the registered agent; the secretarial services master agreement; the current underlying client list; written KYC and AML control policies of the registered agent; and a signed UBO attestation of source of funding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Presence of nominee shareholders, nominee directors, or undisclosed beneficial ownership layers in the Chusik Hoesa.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of the Korean commercial registry extract, electronic shareholder register, and share certificate stubs; signed declarations from any nominee revealing the underlying principal; irrevocable legal documentation confirming ownership; termination proof for any bearer-type instruments; the corporate tax ID certificate; and notarized UBO declarations for every natural person holding or controlling 25% or more.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound funding originates from high-risk, crypto-fiat, or FATF-monitored jurisdictions, creating a potentially unexplained-wealth red flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve or more months of bank statements for each funding shareholder; a source-of-wealth narrative supported by sale contracts, inheritance documents, payroll records, audited financial statements, or tax returns; crypto-to-fiat conversion records if applicable; negative-news screening summaries; and written assurance that the transfer corridors do not involve sanctioned counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Material mismatch between the stated corporate secretarial scope and expected transaction volumes, counterparty profiles, or cross-border treasury flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A rolling twelve-month business plan with monthly projected invoicing and settlement flows; physical office lease or ownership proof; staffing payroll and outsourcing agreements; executed client engagement letters with fee schedules; explanation of any anticipated intercompany funding; evidence of segregated client money handling; and documented AML training and transaction-monitoring procedures.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity remittances must be sent via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 from a depository bank acceptable to the receiving Korean licensed bank, with the remitter legal name, share subscription amount, and shareholder ratio clearly identified. The receiving bank must map the remittance to the BOK foreign exchange purpose code for an inward direct investment equity subscription; the phrase foreign direct investment equity capital contribution must appear in SWIFT field 70. The Korean entity must file the advance foreign investment report through KOTRA or the delegated foreign exchange bank and obtain a certificate of foreign investment registration if the shareholder is an overseas company. The certificate number should be included in the instruction for FEBS reporting. Funds are credited to a temporary capital-verification escrow account, and a certified accountant issues the capital-verification report once the subscription amount matches the paid-in capital registered with the Korean registry. No reliance is placed on unlicensed third-party credits or personal account transfers.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For settled invoices, use SWIFT MT103 with a transaction narrative matching the underlying contract or commercial service; the Korean bank will execute KRW conversion and file the outbound foreign exchange purpose code for commercial service or investment-related payments. For imports of physical goods, commercial letters of credit are opened via MT700/MT710, while documentary collections are executed through MT400/MT410 or correspondent bank courier instructions. Standing settlement instructions, receiving bank BICs, invoice copies, packing lists, and transport documents must be maintained on the bank file to support the trade-payment purpose code. No cash, anonymous clearing, or unregulated third-party settlement rails are permitted.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD, KRW/EUR, and KRW/JPY deliverable forward contracts with a firm underlying trade or service exposure evidenced by invoices and contracts

Offshore nondeliverable forward (NDF) contracts for KRW against USD, EUR, CNH, or JPY where the counterparty and settlement venue are legally permissible and the hedge is limited to documented cross-border exposure
Cross-currency swaps matching the tenor of an inbound capital injection, shareholder loan, or trade-financing facility, limited by the bank's credit line and foreign exchange transaction reporting
FX option strategies restricted to bought options or zero-premium structures used solely to hedge committed invoices, with no naked speculative option writing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements, business report, and regular shareholders' meeting approval under the Korean Commercial Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company general meeting; approved statements retained at the registered office and made available on demand to the National Tax Service and the court registration office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of each fiscal year; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, by March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to convene the regular shareholders' meeting or to present statutory financial statements are subject to administrative fines under the Commercial Act; persistent dormancy may lead to court-ordered dissolution and disruption of tax filings, triggering compulsory collection measures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent certified public accountant audit report and financial statement disclosure via DART
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service through the Data Analysis, Retrieval and Transfer System; audit report attached to the National Tax Service corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For mandatory-audit companies, the external auditor's report must be issued before the regular shareholders' meeting, filed with the FSS through DART within two weeks after the auditor's report date, and attached to the corporate tax return by March 31 for December fiscal year-ends
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor or file the statutory audit report may trigger criminal fines up to KRW 50,000,000 and director liability under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; breach is published by the supervisory authority and may lead to serious tax filing sanctions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporation tax return on taxable income and tax adjustment schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service via HomeTax electronic filing portal and the competent regional tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the last day of the third month after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year company, by March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or unfaithful filing attracts an additional tax of up to 20% of the unpaid corporation tax and a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.022% on unpaid amounts; chronic delinquency may lead to asset seizure, business closure, and court-ordered dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local corporate income tax surtax return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local government treasury in the district of the registered office; filed through the Local Tax e-filing system or joint corporation tax filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same date as the national corporate income tax return: March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The Local Tax Act imposes a 20% additional tax and daily late-payment interest of 0.022% for underpaid or unfiled local surtax; continued delinquency may result in property seizure, business suspension, and revocation of business registration

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-added tax preliminary and final returns for all monthly or quarterly VAT registration cycles
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service via HomeTax VAT filing module
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Preliminary returns for January-March by April 25 and July-September by October 25; final returns for January-June by July 25 and July-December by January 25
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: VAT Act additional taxes of 0.5% to 2% of the relevant taxable supply value apply for late filing or under-declaration, together with daily interest on unpaid VAT; persistent non-filing may lead to criminal referral, compulsory collection, and closures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-invested enterprise status declaration and change report covering foreign ownership and ultimate beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy / Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency or a designated foreign-exchange bank in Korea
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any share transfer, capital change, change in foreign-invested enterprise status, or change in ultimate beneficial ownership; if no chargeable event occurs, there is no fixed annual calendar filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-reporting or late reporting may invalidate foreign-investment tax incentives, attract fines under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and in aggravated cases lead to administrative cancellation of foreign-investment registration

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory statutory audit by a certified public accountant licensed in Korea is required if the entity is a listed company; is a financial institution or financial holding company; or has total assets of at least KRW 12 billion at fiscal year-end. Turnover and headcount are not standalone statutory audit triggers under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, but they are used in SME accounting exemptions and large-company designation under Korea's fair trade disclosure framework.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) apply to listed companies and financial institutions; unlisted companies may apply K-IFRS or Korean GAAP; small and mid-sized companies may apply the SME Accounting Standards issued by the Korean Accounting Standards Board. Statutory audited financial statements must accompany the corporate income tax return and, when the company is subject to external audit, be disclosed through DART.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not require a standalone annual UBO confirmation return for a Chusik Hoesa. Instead, a foreign-invested company and its registered agent must maintain a current beneficial ownership schedule at the registered office and file a change report with KOTRA/MOTIE or a designated foreign-exchange bank within 30 days of any share transfer or UBO change. The National Tax Service, court registry, and Korea Financial Intelligence Unit may demand production of the UBO register on inspection; failure to maintain or deliver the register attracts administrative fines, loss of foreign-investment incentives, and adverse regulatory findings.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Register of Charges/Mortgages, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22% (base corporate rate for taxable income above KRW 20 billion; 10% on first KRW 200 million, 20% on next KRW 19.8 billion, 22% above; plus 10% local income tax surtax resulting in aggregate top effective rate of 24.2%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday for corporate secretarial or registered agent business. General incentives available to SMEs: 5%–10% income deduction for small corporations meeting domestic business substance conditions; limited venture company capital gains exemptions; employment and R&D tax credits. None are special-purpose offshore or registered-agent reliefs.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return (Bub-in-se Gong-gyeo Form, standard Form 1) filed electronically via Hometax (www.hometax.go.kr); International Transaction Information Report (Form 40) submitted with the same filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly prepayment returns (Form 0) for corporations with prior-year taxable income exceeding KRW 50 billion or for larger businesses by interim tax rules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual corporate tax return must be filed within 3 months after the fiscal year-end (March 31 for calendar-year corporations); on request, a 1-month extension may be granted for foreign-owned branches or complex cases. Quarterly prepayments are due within 2 months of each quarter-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business registration number, corporation name, fiscal year-end, industry code (KSC 82990), and resident agent details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Korean domestic place of business address, registered agent name, and electronic filing certifier. For fully non-resident managed entities, provide the local tax representative code and ensure all correspondence reaches a valid Korean address.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assets, paid-in capital, retained earnings, and current liabilities per balance sheet.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Comply with Korean GAAP / IFRS as adopted. If the company holds bank accounts in excess of KRW 50 million, attach bank certificate evidence. Office-sharing arrangements should disclose cost allocation to avoid false substance assertions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 – Tax base calculation (adjustable gross income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue minus deductible expenses, non-deductible amounts, tax-exempt income, and unappropriated retained earnings adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Secretarial and registered agent fees must be recognized on an accrual basis. Deductibility of management fees paid to offshore affiliates requires arm's length justification and statutory supporting agreements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of progressive rates to taxable income: 10% up to KRW 200 million; 20% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion; 22% above KRW 20 billion.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident-owned corporation, no different rate applies. Local income tax at 10% of the corporate tax is declared in the same filing. No dividend deduction is available.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 – Tax credits and foreign tax credit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed credits: foreign tax credit, tax credit for hiring, investment tax credit, and prior-year settlements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim credits only with documentary evidence, including TRC-certified foreign tax payments. Avoid claiming tax-holiday credits not grounded in an approved statutory incentive; automatic credits are subject to anti-abuse review.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 – Net tax payable after prepayments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate tax payable after quarterly prepayments, withholding domestic credits, and excess previous payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Wire transfer execution must be from a Korean domestic bank account registered with the National Tax Service. For companies with no active Korean revenue, file a nil return with a detailed narrative of the zero tax base to avoid automatic penalty assessments.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 20% of unpaid tax for registration-based failures; additional negligence penalty of 20% on understated tax if fraud is shown. Surcharge interest accumulates at 0.025% per day for partial payments after the statutory due date. Non-filing for longer than 6 months triggers tax assessment plus 40% penalty and criminal referral; administrative fines up to KRW 50 million for material misrepresentations.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate (statutory dividend withholding tax 20% under the Personal Income Tax Act as applicable to non-resident shareholders, plus 10% local income tax surtax = 2%, resulting in 22% total on gross dividends).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced DTA dividend rate, the Korean paying company must obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) from the shareholder's resident tax authority and submit it together with Form 24A – Application for Exemption or Reduction of Tax under a Tax Convention to the local tax office before or within 30 days of payment. The withholding agent applies the reduced rate if approval is obtained; otherwise the shareholder may file a non-resident tax return within 3 years to claim a refund. Required attachments: TRC, latest financials, board minutes declaring the dividend, and a shareholder beneficial-ownership declaration.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates for non-resident royalty and interest income are identical to dividends: 20% plus local surtax = 22% aggregate. Under the Korea-US DTA and most OECD agreements, arm's length interest and technical-service royalties are reduced to 10%, and license royalties for copyrights/patents often to 10% or 15% depending on the treaty; Korea-Japan and Korea-China treaties often provide 10% for interest and 10% for royalties. Reduced rates are subject to Limitation on Benefits provisions and require the same TRC application protocol as dividends.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required for Korean corporations that have intra-group transactions with foreign related parties exceeding KRW 5 billion per counterparty per fiscal year or aggregate cross-border related-party transactions exceeding KRW 10 billion. Master File required for multinational groups where the Korean constituent entity's annual turnover is at least KRW 100 billion or the global group consolidated revenue exceeds KRW 1 trillion. Submission of an International Transaction Information Report (Form 40) is mandatory for all domestic entities with related-party transactions exceeding KRW 1 billion per foreign counterparty.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Korea has no general Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) in the Caribbean/Bahrain sense, but the tax authorities apply a statutory substance-over-form doctrine in performing capital amendments and deductions, CFC anti-deferral rules for offshore subsidiaries, and GAAR. For a registered agent / corporate secretarial entity, economic substance is tested by physical office presence, resident staff, independently maintained accounting records, and actual commercial management in Korea. Merely retaining a statutory registered office without substantive functions invokes anti-abuse denial of treaty benefits, a nil-imposition or deemed income adjustment, and possible reclassification of fees as dividends for WHT purposes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion – deliberate understatement or non-filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting fee income from registered-agent or secretarial services, creating false invoices, or maintaining financial records outside Korea to suppress taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Up to 40% assessed additional penalty on the evaded tax, daily late payment surcharge at 0.025%, plus criminal referral under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act: imprisonment up to 2 years or fine up to three times the evaded tax, or both.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax deficiency if assets have been fraudulently diverted. Criminal conviction may result in travel bans, seizure of passports, and a prison sentence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registering the Korean Chusik Hoesa solely to issue inflated service invoices or hold bank accounts while actual management and economic activity occur abroad with no office, no employees, no board meetings, and no commercial rationale in Korea.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax authorities may disregard the entity's separate existence, deny all claimed deductions, re-characterize receipts as deemed dividends, and impose a 22% final withholding tax. Moreover, the National Tax Service may issue a refusal of the business registration and levy a KRW 20 million administrative fine for false registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the shell's assets are transferred to shareholders or offshore related parties before settlement, directors and controlling shareholders are personally liable up to the transferred amount under the Corporate Restructuring Promotion Act and civil debt collection principles; recurring abuse triggers anti-money laundering supervision, asset freezes, and travel restrictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's length management fees or service fees charged by the Korean entity to a foreign parent or affiliate, especially when services are duplicative, undocumented, or performed by offshore personnel.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income adjustment under the International Tax Adjustment Act; penalty of 30% on the under-reported amount; additional interest charge of 8.75% per annum; and dissolution of claimed expense deductions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly execute intra-group agreements that lack arm's length pricing are jointly liable for the additional corporate tax if the arrangement was materially manipulated to strip profits from Korea. Criminal sanctions up to 5 years for intentional violation of reporting obligations apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the registered-agent structure to conceal actual beneficiaries, including nominee shareholders or directors, while receiving fees for offshore secretarial services that facilitate money laundering, tax evasion, or unlicensed financial services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Violation of the Financial Transactions Action Act (AML/CFT) and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act: imprisonment up to 10 years and fines up to KRW 300 million (or 3 times laundered amounts). The Korean Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) may order shutdown of the entity and revocation of resident registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors acting as nominee officers face criminal indictment; any dividends or distinctive benefit received while the company operated as an instrument of financial crime are recoverable personally. Courts regularly impose travel bans and a ban from serving as a director of any Korean company for 5-10 years.
